title: Transactional Fraud
description: Automated analysis of card fraud alerts. An agent weighs the evidence, determines the risk level and issues a verdict justified factor by factor.
problem: Fraud alerts arrive in volume and require judgment, not just rules. The system prepares the case file in code and delegates the judgment to the agent, which must back every factor with the exact data point from the case so the analyst can verify it.

architecture.caption: Five layers: source and consumption, application service, analysis engine, data, and security with observability.

nodes.name: External system
nodes.detail: Raw alert authenticated by API key

nodes.name: Analyst console
nodes.detail: Confirms, dismisses or escalates the alert

nodes.name: Azure Container Apps
nodes.detail: Returns 202 and analyzes in the background

nodes.name: Batch analysis
nodes.detail: Bulk reprocessing over cases in Blob

nodes.name: Azure AI Foundry
nodes.detail: Analyst agent: sets level and writes the verdict

flow: An external system sends the raw alert to the ingestion endpoint, authenticated with an API key. The service responds immediately without blocking the sender.
Analysis starts in the background: the transaction engine compares the operation against the spending profile and measures deviations in amount, channel and time.
The analyst agent, hosted on Azure AI Foundry, receives those facts and decides the risk level by weighing the evidence.
It issues the verdict: executive summary, risk factors with their exact data point, assigned level and recommendations.
The verdict is stored in Cosmos DB along with the case. The process is idempotent: if the verdict already exists, it is not reprocessed.
In parallel, the batch-analysis module reuses the same service to reprocess cases in Blob Storage unattended.

insight.title: Splitting work between code and agent
insight.text: The code does not judge: it prepares the case file. The agent is the one that weighs the evidence and sets the risk level, reasoning over the combination of signals instead of adding up fixed points. Requiring justification makes the verdict reviewable: the analyst receives the full argument, not an opaque verdict.
